newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady amid firm demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady amid firm demand.

text.p: Physical prices of wholesale electricity in the southeastern U.S. finished Tuesday steady against Monday's levels amid firm demand in the southern part of region, market sources said.
"Weather hasn't been too mild...There's still some heat," said one Houston trader.
Today's forecasts showed temperatures in the lower portion of the Southeast topping in the mid-80's to 90 Fahrenheit degree range and bottoming in mid-60's to 70.

In the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC), peak, firm electricity during heavy load hours on Wednesday for delivery into the northern part of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) distribution system was assessed at $14.00-$15.00 a megawatt (MWh), flat from Monday's range.
Off-peak, firm power prices for Wednesday in northern TVA were discussed near $12.00, compared with Monday's quote of $10.00-$12.00.
At the Georgia-Florida border, peak, firm electricity for Wednesday was valued at $22.00-$23.00, higher than Monday's range of $22.00-$22.50.
Utilities in the Virginia and Carolinas were reportedly selling peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday delivery at $18.75-$19.00 a MWh.
TVA was heard offering peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday at $17.50 a MWh, compared with Monday's $18.00 for Tuesday.

Florida Power Corp's 825 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level, Fla., and Duke Power Co's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear station in Seneca, S.C., continued to be out of service, with no restart dates.
